items.title: Louis Keppard Interview, 1961-01-19
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] I think you met Los Angeles finally. He died out there. [INTERVIEWEE] Exactly.

ctx.x: Then what happened to him is he went too far, I guess. And the wildestad, that he takes and went and started fooling around, fooling around. After he got so bright on clarinet, and so perfect on a clarinet, and making the baby cry, and all that, and the other fellows were having a good time. So he figured he'd have a good time. And after that, they found him out that they said, when we called for a white band, we want some white band. We don't want a colored band. So that would knock him out. So after you're…
I think you met Los Angeles finally. He died out there.

Exactly. But I know that's the trouble today, that they found it out. They was colored, and they know it all the time. But as long as he was in his place, he was solid. But the minute that he overcome his jurisdiction, then he takes and he fell down. Like the old words say, who fell down, stayed down. So he went down. And he had to get out of the band. Then he takes and go to California somewhere, as I don't exactly know. But I knew he hurt his own self in the band. So any other thing, Mr.
